mainTopic: The need for התראה, the case of עדים זוממין against a betrothed girl, and which contradictions between witnesses ruin their testimony
overview: The amud finishes the sources showing that a court needs התראה (a warning) before it can punish. One verse is applied to מלקות, and the schools of חזקיה, רבי ישמעאל and רבי each bring a פסוק of their own. The גמרא explains why each source is needed: one for lashes, one for סייף and one for סקילה. It then explains why there are two stoning sources, once according to רבי שמעון and once according to רבנן. Next it finds the source that the sinner must accept death ('יומת המת'). רב חנן teaches that עדים זוממין against a נערה המאורסה are not killed, because they can say they only meant to forbid her to her husband. That rule leads to a long discussion of a learned woman (חברה) and of testimony that cannot be subject to הזמה. רב חסדא then rules which disagreements between witnesses ruin their testimony, and he defends his rule against several challenges, including בן זכאי checking fig stems. The amud ends by asking who בן זכאי was. The answer is that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was still a student when this happened, and that sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The extra verse is applied to lashes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its earlier derivation. The verse cannot be teaching about כרת, so its lesson about warning is applied to מלקות instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: Apply it to the matter of lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a source it was building just before this point. The verse's lesson about warning gets applied to מלקות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line is the 'landing spot' of the earlier argument. The verse could not be about its plain topic (כרת), so its lesson is moved to the topic of מלקות. The result is that the court needs התראה before it can give lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: Apply it to the topic of. Used when a verse is not needed for its plain subject, so it teaches about a different subject.
A warning given to a sinner before he sins, needed before the court can punish him

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new idea starting here. It is the last words of an argument that began before this section, so read it as the ending of that earlier derivation.

phrases.english: Apply it to the matter of lashes.
phrases.notes: 'It' is the פסוק from the earlier argument. It can't be about its plain topic, so it teaches that lashes need a warning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the derivation for התראה that began before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The verse teaches that התראה is required before מלקות.

steps.title: School of חזקיה: warning learned from the murderer
steps.stepSummary: The school of חזקיה learns התראה from the פסוק about a murderer who acts 'intentionally.' The witnesses can only know he meant it if they warned him and he went ahead anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of חזקיה taught: 'But if a man comes intentionally upon his neighbor to kill him with cunning.' This means they warned him, and he still acted on purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second source for התראה from the school of חזקיה. It is based on the פסוק about a murderer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'intentionally' (יָזִד) is the key. How can a court be sure he did it on purpose? It can only be sure if he was warned and kept going anyway, so the פסוק assumes a warning took place.

phrases.english: The school of Ḥizkiyya taught:
"But if a man comes intentionally upon his neighbor
phrases.notes: שמות 21:14

phrases.english: to kill him with cunning"
meaning that they warned him, and he still acts intentionally.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different source for the same rule of התראה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word 'intentionally' in the murder פסוק shows that the murderer was warned first and acted anyway.

steps.title: School of רבי ישמעאל: warning learned from the wood-gatherer
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל learns התראה from the מקושש. The פסוק says they found him 'gathering,' which shows he kept gathering even after he was warned.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'Those who found him gathering sticks.' This means they warned him, and he was still gathering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third source for התראה from the school of רבי ישמעאל. It is based on the story of the man who gathered wood on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses an ongoing form: he was 'gathering.' The school reads this as showing he kept going even after people warned him. So this case of a death penalty also involved a warning.

keyTerms.meaning: Gathering (sticks); the man who gathered wood on שבת is called the מקושש

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
"Those who found him gathering sticks"
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:33

phrases.english: meaning that they warned him, and he was still gathering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another school brings yet another source for the same rule of התראה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ongoing word 'gathering' shows that the מקושש was warned and kept going.

steps.title: School of רבי: warning learned from 'the matter' of the betrothed young woman
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי learns התראה from the פסוק about a נערה המאורסה. The word 'דְּבַר' (matter) hints at 'דִּיבּוּר' (speech), which teaches that the punishment depends on a spoken warning.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי taught: 'For the matter that he humbled.' This means matters that involve speech.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a fourth source for התראה, this one from the school of רבי, based on a word in the פסוק. With this step the list of sources ends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word דְּבַר ('matter') sounds like דִּיבּוּר ('speech'). The school reads this as a hint that the punishment comes only after spoken words, meaning a spoken warning. So this source rests on a word-play, while the earlier sources rested on the meaning of the verbs.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא)

steps.whatToRemember: There are four sources for התראה: (1) a leftover verse applied to מלקות, (2) 'intentionally' by the murderer, (3) 'gathering' by the מקושש, and (4) 'דְּבַר' read as 'דִּיבּוּר' by the נערה המאורסה. They all reach the same rule: no punishment by בית דין without a warning.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi taught:
"For the matter that he humbled"
phrases.notes: דברים 22:24

phrases.english: meaning for matters involving speech.
phrases.notes: The word דְּבַר sounds like דִּיבּוּר, speech. So the punishment comes only after a spoken warning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fourth school gives its own source for התראה, closing the list of sources.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'דְּבַר' hints at 'דִּיבּוּר', so the punishment requires a spoken warning.

steps.title: Why the murderer verse is needed beyond the lashes verse
steps.stepSummary: If the Torah had written התראה only by אחותו, we would think it applies only to מלקות and not to מיתות בית דין. So the Torah also wrote כי יזיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: All these sources are needed. If the Torah wrote only 'his sister,' I would think only people facing lashes need a warning, but not people facing the death penalty. So the Torah wrote 'if a man comes intentionally.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining why we need more than one source for התראה. Here it shows why the murderer verse is needed on top of the lashes verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse of אחותו (step 1) teaches התראה for מלקות. We might think that a much worse sin, one punished by death, needs no warning at all. כי יזיד (step 2) is about a murderer, who gets the death penalty, so it shows that even מיתות need התראה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary. This opens a list showing why each source is needed.
I would have said. This introduces a mistaken idea we might have had.
People liable to a court-imposed death penalty
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah

phrases.english: And it is necessary, for if the Merciful One had written only "his sister" –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 20:17, the lashes source from step 1.

phrases.english: I would have said:
Those liable to lashes – yes, they need a warning,
those liable to death – no.
So the Merciful One wrote "if a man comes intentionally."
phrases.notes: שמות 21:14, the murderer verse from step 2.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the multiple sources listed in steps 1-4 are not redundant.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The source for מלקות alone could not teach that מיתות need התראה. That requires כי יזיד.

steps.title: Why a stoning source is needed beyond the murderer verse
steps.stepSummary: If the Torah had written only כי יזיד, we would think התראה applies only to the lighter death penalty of סייף and not to the harsher סקילה. So a stoning source is needed too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the Torah wrote only 'if a man comes intentionally,' I would think that applies only to the sword, which is lighter, but not to stoning, which is harsher. So it is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues its list. It shows why we also need a source from a stoning case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A murderer is killed by סייף, which counts as a lighter death penalty. We might think the harshest penalty, סקילה, needs no warning. So the stoning sources (the מקושש from step 3 and the נערה המאורסה from step 4) are needed.
steps.whatToRemember: Each source covers a level of punishment the one before it could not: מלקות, then סייף, then סקילה.

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written only "if a man comes intentionally,"
I would have said: this applies only to
the sword, which is lenient,
but stoning, which is severe –
say it does not need a warning. So it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation that began in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The source for סייף alone could not teach that סקילה needs התראה, so a stoning source is required.

steps.title: Why are there two stoning sources?
steps.stepSummary: The מקושש and the נערה המאורסה are both stoning cases. Why do we need both?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need two sources from cases of stoning?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why there are two stoning sources, since one seems to be enough. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 showed that one stoning source is needed. But the מקושש (step 3) and the נערה המאורסה (step 4) are both punished with סקילה, so one of them looks extra.

phrases.english: And why do I need two sources among those who are stoned?
phrases.notes: He means the מקושש (step 3) and the נערה המאורסה (step 4).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 6 and asks about the extra stoning source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the second stoning source teach?

steps.title: According to רבי שמעון, the extra source teaches about burning
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון holds that שריפה is harsher than סקילה. So the extra stoning source teaches that even those punished with burning need התראה.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי שמעון, it comes to include those who are burned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer, which follows the view of רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון, שריפה is the harshest death penalty, even harsher than stoning. So we might think it needs no warning. The second stoning source is used to cover שריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who holds that burning is harsher than stoning

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Shimon, it comes to include those who are burned.
phrases.notes: The גמרא assumes we know רבי שמעון's view that burning is harsher than stoning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 7 according to רבי שמעון.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra stoning source teaches that שריפה also needs התראה.

steps.title: According to רבנן, the Torah sometimes writes what a קל וחומר could teach
steps.stepSummary: רבנן hold that סקילה is the harshest penalty, so שריפה could be learned by קל וחומר. Even so, the Torah sometimes writes out such a rule anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the Rabbis, the Torah sometimes takes the trouble to write out something that could be learned through a קל וחומר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer, which follows רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבנן, stoning is harsher than burning. If even stoning needs a warning, then burning surely does, so no extra source seems needed for שריפה. The answer is that the Torah sometimes writes something out even though it could be learned by logic. So the second stoning source still teaches about שריפה, even though a קל וחומר could have taught the same thing.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, who hold that stoning is harsher than burning
A logical argument from lighter to heavier
The verse took the trouble to write it out

steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not find a new law in the extra source. It accepts that the Torah sometimes writes out something we could have figured out on our own.

phrases.english: According to the Rabbis,
a matter that could be derived through a קל וחומר –
the verse took the trouble and wrote it anyway.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרַבָּנַן, מִילְּתָא דְּאָתְיָא בְּקַל וָחוֹמֶר טָרַח וְכָתַב לַהּ קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to step 7, according to רבנן.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second stoning source is a case where the Torah writes out something a קל וחומר could teach.

steps.title: Then why not write the rule only by stoning?
steps.stepSummary: If stoning is the harshest penalty, the Torah could have written התראה only there and learned everything else from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then let the Torah write it only by those who are stoned, and let the other cases be learned from it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the system of sources itself, now that stoning is treated as the harshest penalty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבנן, סקילה is the harshest penalty. So a stoning source alone should teach, by קל וחומר, that every lighter punishment needs התראה too. This makes אחותו and כי יזיד look unnecessary, which goes against the צריכותא of steps 5-6.

keyTerms.meaning: And let them be learned from it

phrases.english: But let the Merciful One write it only among those who are stoned,
and let those others come and be learned from it?
phrases.notes: "Those others" means the lashes and sword cases, אחותו and כי יזיד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the צריכותא of steps 5-6, building on רבנן's view in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in steps 5-6 that אחותו and כי יזיד are each needed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If stoning is the harshest penalty, a single stoning source teaches all lighter cases by קל וחומר.

steps.title: The same answer: the Torah writes it out anyway
steps.stepSummary: Here too, the Torah took the trouble to write out rules that could have been learned by קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, the Torah takes the trouble to write out something that could be learned through a קל וחומר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with the same idea it used in step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is true that the other sources could be learned from stoning. Still, the Torah chose to write each one out, just as it does in other places. So having several sources is not a problem.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבנן, the extra sources for התראה are explained by one idea: the Torah sometimes writes out what logic could already teach.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי, מִילְּתָא דְּאָתְיָא בְּקַל וָחוֹמֶר
phrases.english: Here too, a matter that could be derived through a קל וחומר –
the verse took the trouble and wrote it anyway.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי, מִילְּתָא דְּאָתְיָא בְּקַל וָחוֹמֶר טָרַח וְכָתַב לַהּ קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applies the same principle used in step 9
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra sources look pointless, because stoning alone would teach everything.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah sometimes writes out rules that a קל וחומר could have taught, so the extra sources are acceptable.

steps.title: Where do we learn that the sinner must accept death?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule that the sinner must 'release himself to death.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The sinner must 'release himself to death.' Where do we learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up a detail from the warning process: the sinner must say he accepts death. It asks where this rule comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The steps before this one showed that a warning (התראה) is needed. Here the גמרא adds one more detail: the sinner has to openly accept the punishment. The question asks for the source of this added detail.

keyTerms.meaning: He 'released himself to death.' He said he accepts that he will be killed and sins anyway.
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: He released himself to death,
phrases.notes: After the warning, he answers that he knows the penalty is death and will sin anyway.

phrases.english: from where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the sources for התראה to a further detail of the warning process.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for requiring the sinner to accept death.

steps.title: The source: 'the dead shall be put to death'
steps.stepSummary: רבא (or חזקיה) learns it from the words 'יומת המת.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said, and some say it was חזקיה: The פסוק says 'the dead shall be put to death.' This means he is not killed until he releases himself to death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק that calls the sinner 'the dead one' even before he is executed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling a living person 'dead' tells us he already treated himself as dead. He accepted the death penalty when he was warned. That is why the פסוק requires him to 'release himself to death.'

keyTerms.meaning: 'The dead shall be put to death' (דברים 17:6)
And some say. It gives a second opinion about who said the statement.

phrases.english: Rava said, and some say it was Ḥizkiyya:
The verse states: "The dead shall be put to death" –
phrases.notes: דברים 17:6

phrases.english: meaning, not until he releases himself to death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'יומת המת' call him 'dead' before his execution, which teaches that he must accept death first.

steps.title: רב חנן: lying witnesses against a betrothed girl are not killed
steps.stepSummary: עדים זוממין who testified against a נערה המאורסה are not executed, because they can say they only meant to forbid her to her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנן said: Witnesses who testified against a betrothed young woman and were proven to be עדים זוממין are not killed. This is because they can say, 'We came only to make her forbidden to her husband.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנן gives a new rule. It is an exception to the usual punishment of עדים זוממין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally עדים זוממין receive the punishment they tried to bring on the accused. Here the witnesses can claim they only wanted her forbidden to her husband, not killed. So they are not executed.

keyTerms.meaning: Plotting witnesses. They are proven false because other witnesses show they were somewhere else at the time.
A betrothed young woman. If she sins with another man, her penalty is סקילה.
Who were proven to be זוממין
To make her forbidden to her husband

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean they stop being עדים זוממין. It is only an exception in how their punishment is carried out.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥanan says:
Witnesses against a betrothed young woman who were proven to be conspiring witnesses
are not killed,
because they can say:
"We came to forbid her to her husband."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חָנָן: עֵדֵי נַעֲרָה הַמְאוֹרָסָה שֶׁהוּזַּמּוּ אֵין נֶהֱרָגִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new statement about the betrothed girl, connected to the discussion of התראה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עדים זוממין against a נערה המאורסה are not executed, because they can claim their goal was only to forbid her to her husband.

steps.title: But they warned her
steps.stepSummary: The witnesses gave her a warning that mentioned the death penalty, so how can they say they did not mean to have her killed?
steps.simpleTranslation: But they warned her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חנן's reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A warning tells the sinner the punishment, which here is death. If the witnesses warned her, they clearly knew their testimony would lead to her death. So their claim of 'we only meant to forbid her' does not hold up.

phrases.english: But they forewarned her!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning of step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חנן's reason that the witnesses can say they only meant to forbid her
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A warning mentions death, so the witnesses cannot claim they did not intend to have her executed.

steps.title: The case is where they did not warn her
steps.stepSummary: רב חנן is talking about a case with no warning.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is where they did not warn her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by saying רב חנן's case had no warning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With no warning, nothing shows that the witnesses were aiming for her death. So their claim is believable.

phrases.english: It is a case where they did not forewarn her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed the witnesses had warned her.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב חנן's case is one where no warning was given.

steps.title: Without a warning, how could she be killed?
steps.stepSummary: Without התראה she could not be executed anyway, so there is nothing new in רב חנן's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if they did not warn her, how can she be killed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer it just gave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without a warning, the court would never execute her. If so, the witnesses also could not be killed, since they did not try to bring about a death sentence. רב חנן's rule would then teach nothing new.

phrases.english: But if they did not forewarn her,
how can she be killed?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי לָא אַתְרוֹ בַּהּ, הֵיכִי מִיקַּטְלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the case had no warning
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without התראה there is no death penalty, so there is nothing for the witnesses to be spared from.

steps.title: The case is a learned woman, following רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The woman is a חברה, a learned woman, and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds that such a person can be executed without a warning.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is a woman who is a חברה, and the rule follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the problem. The woman is learned in Torah, and according to one תנא she can be executed even without a warning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer explains both sides. She can be executed without a warning, so the witnesses did try to bring about her death. But they never warned her, so they can still claim they only meant to forbid her to her husband.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who is learned in Torah law

phrases.english: It is a case of a woman who is a ḥavera,
phrases.notes: A חברה is someone who knows Torah law well.

phrases.english: and it follows the opinion of Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּאִשָּׁה חֲבֵירָה, וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17 by narrowing רב חנן's case further.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to follow one opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without a warning, no one can be executed.
steps.terutzMaskana: A learned woman can be executed without a warning according to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, so רב חנן's rule teaches something.

steps.title: The ברייתא of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds a חבר needs no warning, because a warning is only meant to show whether he sinned on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says, a חבר does not need a warning. This is because a warning is given only to tell apart someone who sinned by accident from someone who sinned on purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the source of the opinion it just relied on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, the only job of a warning is to prove the sinner knew what he was doing. A learned person surely knew, so the warning is not needed.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: רב חנן's rule works only for a learned woman, and only according to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who holds that the warning just proves the sin was on purpose.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows two ways to understand התראה. One view says it is just proof of intent. The other says it is a formal requirement, where the sinner must accept death.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says:
A ḥaver does not require forewarning,
because forewarning was given
only to distinguish between unintentional and intentional sinning.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: חָבֵר אֵין צָרִיךְ הַתְרָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the source for the opinion used in step 18.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds a learned person can be executed without a warning
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה

steps.title: How can she be killed if the witnesses can never be punished?
steps.stepSummary: If the witnesses can never be killed as עדים זוממין, their testimony cannot be subject to הזמה, and such testimony is not valid testimony at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the witnesses are not killed, how can she be killed? Their testimony is testimony you cannot make into false-witness testimony, and any testimony like that is not counted as testimony.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a challenge. If the witnesses are safe from punishment, how can the woman be executed based on what they said?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a basic rule: testimony only counts if the witnesses could be punished through הזמה if they lied. Here the witnesses can always escape by saying they only meant to forbid her to her husband. So their testimony seems to fail that basic rule, and she should not be killable.

keyTerms.meaning: Proving witnesses to be false by showing they were somewhere else at the time; such witnesses are then punished
Testimony that could never lead to punishing the witnesses as false witnesses
It is not considered valid testimony

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up who is being punished. 'They' are the witnesses; 'she' is the woman they testified about.

phrases.english: And since they are not killed,
phrases.notes: 'They' means the witnesses, who escape punishment by saying they only meant to forbid her to her husband.

phrases.english: how can she be killed?
It is testimony
that you cannot render conspiratory,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל עֵדוּת שֶׁאִי אַתָּה יָכוֹל לַהֲזִימָּהּ
phrases.english: and any testimony that you cannot render conspiratory
is not called testimony.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵיוָן דְּאִינְהוּ לָא מִיקַּטְלִי, אִיהִי הֵיכִי מִיקַּטְלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the case of a חברה established in steps 18-19 and attacks the idea that she can be executed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the חברה can be executed in רב חנן's case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Testimony that can never be subject to הזמה is invalid. These witnesses can never be punished, so their testimony should not be enough to kill her.

steps.title: That is exactly רב חנן's point: she is not killed either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב חנן agrees: because the witnesses cannot be punished, the woman is not executed either.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is what he means: since the witnesses are not killed, because they can say 'We came to forbid her to her husband,' she too is not killed, because this testimony cannot be subject to הזמה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the challenge into the explanation. רב חנן's rule is about her too: she is not killed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed רב חנן meant only that the witnesses go free. The answer says his rule has two parts. The witnesses are not killed, and as a result she is not killed, since the testimony against her fails the הזמה rule.

keyTerms.meaning: That is indeed what he is saying
Since; because of the fact that
To make her forbidden to her husband

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the הזמה rule protects the accused, not just the witnesses. If the witnesses can't be punished, the accused can't be punished either.

phrases.english: That is also what he is saying:
phrases.notes: 'He' is רב חנן, whose rule the גמרא has been discussing.

phrases.english: Since they are not killed,
because they can say
'We came to forbid her to her husband,'
she too is not killed,
since it is testimony
that you cannot render conspiratory.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20 by accepting its logic and reading it into רב חנן's statement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the challenge is accepted as the intended meaning of the rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב חנן's rule only freed the witnesses, and the woman would still be executed.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב חנן's rule frees both the witnesses and the woman, because the testimony cannot be subject to הזמה.

steps.title: So when could a חברה ever be executed?
steps.stepSummary: If the witnesses can always use the excuse, the גמרא asks how there can ever be a case where a חברה is executed according to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But for a woman who is a חברה, whom we hold can be killed, how can you find such a case according to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question. If the excuse always works, when would a חברה without a warning ever actually be executed?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says a חברה can be executed without התראה. But without התראה, witnesses can always claim they only meant to forbid her to her husband, which blocks הזמה and so blocks her execution. So it seems his rule could never apply in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: A learned woman, who knows the law, so she needs no warning according to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה
We hold; it is established for us
How can you find such a case?

phrases.english: But with a woman who is a חברה,
whom we hold can be killed,
phrases.notes: He means killed even without a warning, as shown in the ברייתא in step 19.

phrases.english: according to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה
how can you find it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בְּאִשָּׁה חֲבֵירָה, דְּקַיְימָא לַן דְּמִיקַּטְלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 21: if the excuse blocks execution, the case of a חברה seems impossible.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A real case where a חברה can be executed according to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, even though the witnesses would normally have the excuse.

steps.title: When she sinned a second time
steps.stepSummary: The case is where she committed adultery and then did it again, so the witnesses cannot say they came to forbid her to her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: When she committed adultery, and then committed adultery again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The case is about a second act of adultery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the first act, she is already forbidden to her husband. So for the second act, the witnesses cannot claim they meant to forbid her to him, because that already happened. Without the excuse, they can be punished through הזמה, and she can be executed.

keyTerms.meaning: And she went back and committed adultery again

phrases.english: When she committed adultery, and then again committed adultery.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It happens when the testimony is about a second act of adultery, since she is already forbidden to her husband.

steps.title: They could say they came to forbid her to the second man
steps.stepSummary: The witnesses could still claim they only meant to forbid her to the second man she was with.
steps.simpleTranslation: But they can say: 'We came to forbid her to her second partner!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer. The witnesses still have a new excuse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman who commits adultery also becomes forbidden to the man she sinned with, the בועל. So in the second act, the witnesses can say they only wanted to forbid her to this second man. That excuse would again block הזמה.

keyTerms.meaning: The man she had relations with

phrases.english: But they can say:
'We came to forbid her to her second partner!'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא יְכוֹלִין לוֹמַר: לְאוֹסְרָהּ עַל בּוֹעֲלָהּ שֵׁנִי בָּאנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 23 by finding a new excuse for the witnesses.
steps.kashyaTarget: The case of a second act of adultery given in step 23.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The second act makes her forbidden to the second man, so the witnesses can claim that was their goal, and הזמה is still blocked.

steps.title: Same man again, or a close relative
steps.stepSummary: The case is where the second act was with the first man, or with a relative, since she is already forbidden to either one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where she committed adultery again with the first partner, or alternatively, where she committed adultery with one of her relatives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by narrowing the case even more. It gives two cases where the witnesses have no excuse left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the second act was with the same man as the first, she is already forbidden to him. If it was with a relative, she was forbidden to him all along. Either way, the witnesses' testimony makes her forbidden to no one new, so they can be punished through הזמה, and she can be executed.

keyTerms.meaning: The first man she sinned with
Her close relatives, who are forbidden to her anyway

steps.whatToRemember: Testimony counts only if the witnesses could be punished as עדים זוממין. A חברה can be executed without התראה only when the witnesses cannot claim they were just making her forbidden to someone. This happens on a second act with the same man or with a relative.

phrases.english: Where she committed adultery with the first partner,
or alternatively, where she committed adultery with her relatives.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁזִּינְּתָה מִבּוֹעֵל רִאשׁוֹן, אִי נָמֵי שֶׁזִּינְּתָה מִקְּרוֹבֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 24 by limiting the case so no new prohibition can be the witnesses' excuse.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) so the excuse cannot apply.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any second act of adultery would leave the witnesses an excuse about the second man.
steps.terutzMaskana: When the second act is with the same man or a relative, the witnesses have no excuse, so הזמה is possible and she can be executed.

steps.title: Why did רב חנן mention a betrothed girl?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב חנן framed his rule around a נערה המאורסה, since a married woman would work too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did he pick a betrothed young woman? A married woman would also fit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב חנן described his case using a betrothed girl. The witnesses' excuse would seem to work just as well for a fully married woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The witnesses' excuse is 'we only came to forbid her to her husband.' Any married woman has a husband she can be forbidden to. So why limit the case to a נערה המאורסה?

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Why this case specifically?
A betrothed young woman who has not yet moved in with her husband

phrases.english: What is different that he chose a betrothed young woman?
phrases.notes: 'He' is רב חנן, whose rule the גמרא has been discussing.

phrases.english: Even a married woman as well!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defining the case, the גמרא asks about the details of how רב חנן worded his rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב חנן's ruling mentions only a נערה המאורסה and not a married woman.

steps.title: Even a betrothed girl gives the witnesses their excuse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that a married woman is included. The new point is that even a betrothed girl, who does not live with her husband, still gives the witnesses their excuse.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is true. But the point is that even this one, who does not live with him, still lets the witnesses say: we came to forbid her to her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the rule really does apply to a married woman too. Mentioning a betrothed girl teaches something extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think the excuse only makes sense when she actually lives with her husband. רב חנן teaches that even a betrothed girl, who is not yet living with him, is forbidden to him by adultery. So the witnesses can still claim that was their goal.

keyTerms.meaning: Lives 'under' him, meaning she lives with her husband
To make her forbidden to her husband

steps.whatToRemember: רב חנן's rule covers every married woman. He mentioned a betrothed girl to show that the excuse works even when she does not yet live with her husband.

phrases.english: Yes, but
even this one, who does not live under him,
they can say: 'We came to forbid her to her husband.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ הַאי דְּלָא יָתְבָא תּוּתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rule includes married women. The betrothed case teaches that the excuse works even when she does not live with her husband.

steps.title: רב חסדא: disagreeing about the weapon matters, disagreeing about clothing does not
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules on which disagreements between two witnesses ruin their testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא says: if one witness says 'he killed him with a sword' and the other says 'with an אֲרִירָן,' the testimony is not consistent. If one says 'his clothes were black' and the other says 'his clothes were white,' the testimony is still consistent.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב חסדא teaches which disagreements between witnesses make their testimony fail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The weapon is part of the killing itself, so a disagreement about it is a real contradiction. The color of the killer's clothing is a side detail, so a disagreement there does not ruin the testimony.

keyTerms.meaning: Consistent or established. The testimony holds together.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda says:
If one says, 'He killed him with a sword,'
and one says, 'He killed him with an ariran,'
this is not 'consistent.'
phrases.notes: The word נכון comes from the פסוק about testimony, דברים 17:4.

phrases.english: If one says, 'His garments were black,'
and one says, 'His garments were white,'
this is 'consistent.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic about contradictions between witnesses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A disagreement about the weapon ruins the testimony. A disagreement about the color of the killer's clothing does not.

steps.title: A ברייתא says a clothing disagreement also ruins testimony
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא from a ברייתא that treats a clothing-color disagreement as a contradiction.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: 'נכון' means the testimony must be consistent. If one says 'with a sword' and one says 'with an אֲרִירָן,' or one says 'his clothes were black' and one says 'white,' this is not consistent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that seems to argue directly with רב חסדא about the clothing case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא puts the clothing disagreement in the same list as the weapon disagreement. It calls both 'not נכון,' which is the opposite of what רב חסדא said about clothing.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection from a ברייתא

phrases.english: They raised an objection: 'Certain' means that it must be consistent.
phrases.notes: דברים 17:4

phrases.english: If one says, 'He killed him with a sword,'
and one says, 'He killed him with an ariran,'
or one says, 'His garments were black,'
and one says, 'His garments were white,'
this is not 'consistent.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the clothing half of רב חסדא's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's ruling that a clothing-color disagreement is still נכון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא explicitly calls the black-versus-white clothing case 'not נכון.'

steps.title: The clothing in the ברייתא was the murder weapon
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that the ברייתא is talking about a scarf used to strangle the victim, so it counts as a weapon.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא explained it: it is talking about a scarf he strangled him with, which is just like the sword and אֲרִירָן case.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers that the ברייתא's 'garment' was the thing used to kill. Disagreeing about it is the same as disagreeing about the weapon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא's rule stays the same. Only details about the killing itself matter. Here the garment was itself the weapon, so its color is part of the killing and not a side detail.

keyTerms.meaning: He explained it (in a way that fits his view)

phrases.english: Rav Chisda interpreted it:
about a scarf with which he strangled him,
which is the same as sword and ariran.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the ברייתא as a narrower case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say that the color of any clothing matters.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is talking about clothing that was used as the murder weapon.

steps.title: A second ברייתא about sandal color
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another ברייתא saying that a disagreement about the color of the killer's sandals ruins the testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if one says 'his sandals were black' and one says 'his sandals were white,' this is not consistent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge to רב חסדא. This time the disagreement is about the color of the killer's sandals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sandals seem to be an even clearer side detail than clothing. If a disagreement about them ruins the testimony, it looks like רב חסדא is wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear, introducing a source

phrases.english: Come and hear: if one says, 'His sandals were black,'
and one says, 'His sandals were white,'
this is not 'consistent.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second attack on רב חסדא after step 30 answered the first one.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's ruling that side details do not ruin testimony.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Sandal color is a side detail, yet the ברייתא says a disagreement about it makes the testimony not נכון.

steps.title: The sandal was used to kill
steps.stepSummary: Here too, the case is where the killer kicked the victim to death with his sandal.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, it is a case where he kicked him with his sandal and killed him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the same way as before. The sandal was the murder weapon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the sandal is the thing that killed, its color is a detail of the killing itself. That fits רב חסדא's rule exactly.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב חסדא, only disagreements about the killing itself, including the weapon, ruin testimony. Any object used to kill, even a scarf or sandal, counts as the weapon.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think clothing or sandals always matter. They matter only when they were the murder weapon.

phrases.english: There, too,
it is where he kicked him with his sandal and killed him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם נָמֵי, כְּגוֹן שֶׁבָּעַט בּוֹ בְּסַנְדָּלוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 31 the same way step 30 answered step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the ברייתא as a narrower case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sandal color seemed to be a side detail.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sandal was the murder weapon, so its color is a detail of the killing.

steps.title: Challenge from בן זכאי checking fig stems
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא from the משנה, where בן זכאי questioned witnesses about the stems of figs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: There was an incident, and בן זכאי examined the witnesses about the stems of figs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another challenge to רב חסדא, this time from the story in the משנה about בן זכאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fig stems are a small side detail, like the color of clothing. If בן זכאי bothered to check them, a disagreement about them must ruin the testimony. That goes against רב חסדא, who said disagreements about side details do not ruin it.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: an introduction to a proof or challenge from a source
Fig stems, the little stalks that attach the fig to the tree

phrases.english: Come and hear: There was an incident,
phrases.notes: This is quoting the משנה from earlier in the פרק.

phrases.english: and ben Zakkai examined the witnesses about the stems of figs.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: מַעֲשֶׂה, וּבָדַק בֶּן זַכַּאי בְּעוּקְצֵי תְּאֵנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third challenge to רב חסדא, following the clothing and sandal challenges.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's rule that a disagreement about a side detail does not ruin testimony
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בן זכאי checked a minor detail (fig stems), which shows that disagreement on such details does ruin testimony.

steps.title: The crime was picking a fig on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא answers that the case was about someone who picked a fig on שבת, so the fig itself was the crime.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said: The case was where he picked a fig on שבת, and he is being put to death for that act.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא defends רב חסדא by saying the fig in that case was not a side detail at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the death penalty was for picking the fig on שבת, then the fig is the heart of the crime. Questions about it are like questions about the weapon in a murder, so they matter. This fits רב חסדא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who answers the challenge here

phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama said:
For example, where he picked a fig on Shabbat,
since it is for that very act that he is being killed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא: כְּגוֹן שֶׁעָקַץ תְּאֵנָה בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case so the detail becomes central to the crime
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The fig stems were an unimportant side detail.
steps.terutzMaskana: The fig was the crime itself (picking on שבת), so its details matter.

steps.title: But the case was a murder under a fig tree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back with a ברייתא showing the witnesses said he killed the victim under a fig tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: They said to him, 'He killed him under a fig tree.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רמי בר חמא's answer by showing the case was really a murder, not a שבת case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא tells us the witnesses spoke about a killing under a fig tree. So the fig was not the crime, and the answer about picking on שבת does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: But a ברייתא teaches, used to challenge an answer

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a baraita:
They said to him, "He killed him beneath a fig tree"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא תַּנְיָא: אָמְרוּ לוֹ תַּחַת תְּאֵנָה הֲרָגוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 34.
steps.kashyaTarget: רמי בר חמא's explanation that the case was picking a fig on שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא describes a murder under a fig tree, so the case was a killing, not a שבת violation.

steps.title: He stabbed the victim with a fig branch
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא gives a new answer: the killer stabbed the victim with a fig branch, so the fig tree was the weapon.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רמי בר חמא said: The case was where he stabbed him with a branch of a fig tree.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא drops his first answer and gives a new one that still fits רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a fig branch was the murder weapon, then questions about the fig tree are questions about the weapon. רב חסדא agrees that a disagreement about the weapon ruins the testimony, so there is no problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, which signals a new answer replacing the old one
A branch or shoot of a tree

phrases.english: Rather, Rami bar Ḥama said:
For example, where he stabbed him with a branch of a fig tree.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא: כְּגוֹן שֶׁשִּׁפְּדוֹ בְּיִיחוּר שֶׁל תְּאֵנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new answer after step 35 rejected the first one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Making the fig the murder weapon, like the scarf and sandal answers
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case was picking a fig on שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The fig branch was the weapon, so details about it matter.

steps.title: But he asked about the fruit itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that בן זכאי asked about the figs' stems and color, which has nothing to do with a branch used as a weapon.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: He said to them: This fig tree, were its stems thin or thick? Were the figs black or white?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the fig-branch answer by quoting בן זכאי's actual questions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His questions were about the fruit: thin or thick stems, black or white figs. A fruit's color has nothing to do with a branch used to stab someone. So these really were side-detail questions, and the challenge to רב חסדא is back.

phrases.english: Come and hear: He said to them:
phrases.notes: "He" is בן זכאי, speaking to the witnesses.

phrases.english: This fig tree, were its stems thin?
Were its stems thick?
Were the figs black? Were the figs white?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, אָמַר לָהֶן: תְּאֵנָה זוֹ עֳקָצֶיהָ דַּקִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 36.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the fig branch was the weapon
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בן זכאי's questions were about the fruit, which is unrelated to a branch used as a weapon.

steps.title: בן זכאי had his own view
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that we cannot challenge רב חסדא from בן זכאי, because בן זכאי held that side questions count like core questions.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יוסף said: Would anyone raise a challenge from בן זכאי? בן זכאי is different, because he treats בדיקות like חקירות.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives up on explaining the fig case and instead says בן זכאי's opinion is a lone view that we do not follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, disagreement on side questions (בדיקות) does not ruin testimony, but disagreement on core questions (חקירות) does. בן זכאי held that both count the same. רב חסדא follows the regular view, so בן זכאי's practice is no challenge to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Core questions about time and place, where any contradiction ruins the testimony

steps.whatToRemember: The fig-stem story is no proof against רב חסדא, because בן זכאי held a personal view that בדיקות are as serious as חקירות.
steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף is not saying בן זכאי was wrong to ask. He is saying בן זכאי's rule differs from the rule that רב חסדא follows.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Yosef said:
Should a person raise a challenge from ben Zakkai?
Ben Zakkai is different,
since he treats examinations like interrogations.
phrases.notes: Interrogations are the core questions like when and where. Examinations are the extra side-detail questions.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מִבֶּן זַכַּאי לוֹתֵיב אִינִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 37 in a new way after the case-based answers failed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the source to an individual opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בן זכאי's practice shows the general law about side details.
steps.terutzMaskana: בן זכאי held his own stricter view, so he is no challenge to רב חסדא.

steps.title: Who was בן זכאי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who בן זכאי was, and doubts that it was רבי יוחנן בן זכאי, since it is unclear he sat on a סנהדרין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is בן זכאי? If you say it is רבי יוחנן בן זכאי, was he ever on a סנהדרין?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: figuring out who the בן זכאי in the משנה was. It is setting up a timeline problem that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה shows בן זכאי judging a murder case, which needs a סנהדרין. The obvious guess is the famous רבי יוחנן בן זכאי. But the גמרא questions whether he ever served on a סנהדרין that judged such cases.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say, which suggests an answer that will be challenged
The court that judges cases of the death penalty

phrases.english: Who is ben Zakkai?
If we say it is Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Zakkai,
was he ever in a Sanhedrin?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new side topic about the person named in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the בן זכאי mentioned in the משנה

steps.title: The 120 years of רבי יוחנן בן זכאי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that divides רבי יוחנן בן זכאי's 120 years into three forty-year periods, to question whether he sat on a סנהדרין.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: All the years of רבי יוחנן בן זכאי were 120. Forty years he did business, forty years he learned, and forty years he taught.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports its doubt with a ברייתא about רבי יוחנן בן זכאי's life. It is setting up a timeline argument that continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows he only became a teacher and leader in his last forty years. The גמרא will use this to show that his time as a leader may not match a time when a סנהדרין judged death-penalty cases.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שְׁנוֹתָיו שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
phrases.english: All the years of Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Zakkai
were one hundred and twenty years.
Forty years he was engaged in business,
forty years he studied,
forty years he taught.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: כׇּל שְׁנוֹתָיו שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי מֵאָה וְעֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source behind the doubt raised in step 39.
steps.raayaObject: The doubt that רבי יוחנן בן זכאי sat on a סנהדרין judging death-penalty cases
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא describing his 120 years in three forty-year periods

steps.title: The סנהדרין left its chamber forty years before the חורבן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the סנהדרין moved out forty years before the חורבן. רבי יצחק בר אבודימי explains this meant they stopped judging certain cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: forty years before the Temple was destroyed, the סנהדרין was exiled and sat in 'the store.' רבי יצחק בר אבודימי says this means they no longer judged דיני קנסות (cases of fines).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues building its question from step 40. It brings a second source showing that the סנהדרין's power shrank forty years before the חורבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 40 showed only that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was a leader in the last forty years of his life. Now the גמרא adds that the סנהדרין stopped judging certain cases forty years before the חורבן. Step 42 shows these were capital cases, and step 43 shows he was still leading after the חורבן. Together, these show his years as a leader never overlapped with capital cases.

keyTerms.meaning: The destruction of the בית המקדש
The סנהדרין was exiled (moved out of its usual chamber)
'The store', a place outside the סנהדרין's normal chamber
Cases of fines (set penalties the תורה imposes)

phrases.aramaic: וְתַנְיָא: אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה קוֹדֶם חוּרְבַּן הַבַּיִת,
phrases.english: And it is taught in a baraita: Forty years before the destruction of the Temple,
the Sanhedrin was exiled and sat in the store.
phrases.notes: The 'store' is a spot outside the special chamber on the Temple Mount where the סנהדרין normally sat.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak bar Avudimi says:
This comes to say that they no longer judged cases of fines.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא: אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה קוֹדֶם חוּרְבַּן הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second source to the ברייתא of step 40, as part of the same question.
steps.raayaObject: That רבן יוחנן בן זכאי could not have sat on a capital case.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about the סנהדרין moving out forty years before the חורבן, explained by רבי יצחק בר אבודימי.

steps.title: Correcting the statement from fines to capital cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that they stopped judging fines. It corrects the wording: they stopped judging דיני נפשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Could you really think they stopped judging cases of fines? Rather, he meant that they stopped judging capital cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects to the wording of רבי יצחק בר אבודימי's statement and fixes it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Courts kept judging דיני קנסות long after the חורבן, so the statement cannot mean fines. The corrected version says the court lost its power over capital cases once it left its chamber. This correction is exactly what the גמרא needs for its question about judging a murderer.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it enter your mind? (a way of rejecting an idea)

phrases.english: Cases of fines, could that enter your mind?
Rather, he meant that they no longer judged capital cases.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges and corrects the wording of the statement quoted in step 41.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק בר אבודימי's claim that the court stopped judging דיני קנסות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Fines were still judged long after the חורבן, so the statement cannot mean fines.
steps.terutzMaskana: The statement means that the court stopped judging דיני נפשות.

steps.title: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי led after the destruction
steps.stepSummary: A משנה shows that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי made his rulings after the חורבן. This completes the question.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we learned in a משנה: Once the Temple was destroyed, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי made a new ruling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the last piece of its question: a משנה showing that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was a leader after the חורבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His forty years of leading ran past the חורבן. Capital cases had already stopped forty years before the חורבן. So during his years as a leader there were no capital cases at all, and he could not have questioned the witnesses as a judge.

keyTerms.meaning: He made a new ruling (a תקנה)

steps.whatToRemember: Capital cases stopped 40 years before the חורבן, and רבן יוחנן בן זכאי led after it. So he could not have judged a capital case as a leader.

phrases.english: And we learned in a mishna:
Once the Temple was destroyed,
Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai made a new ruling.
phrases.notes: This is from סוכה 41a. It is his ruling that people everywhere should take the לולב all seven days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the last piece needed to finish the question started in step 39.
steps.raayaObject: That רבן יוחנן בן זכאי could not have been a judge in a capital case.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in סוכה about his ruling after the חורבן.

steps.title: It was a different ben Zakkai
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the בן זכאי in the משנה was some other person with that name.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it was just an ordinary person named בן זכאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by saying the בן זכאי in our משנה is not the famous רבן יוחנן בן זכאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the famous sage could not have judged a capital case, the גמרא says the name belongs to someone else. This removes the timing problem completely.

phrases.english: Rather, it was just some ordinary ben Zakkai.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question built up in steps 39 through 43.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בן זכאי is the famous רבן יוחנן בן זכאי.
steps.terutzMaskana: בן זכאי is a different, lesser-known person.

steps.title: The plain name supports a different person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the answer: רבי would not call the great רבן יוחנן בן זכאי just 'בן זכאי.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This makes sense too. If it were רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, would רבי call him just 'בן זכאי'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer from the way the משנה words the name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A great sage would be named with his title and first name. Writing only 'בן זכאי' sounds like someone less famous. This supports the answer in step 44.

keyTerms.meaning: So too it is reasonable (support for an answer)

phrases.english: So too it is reasonable,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי,
phrases.english: for if it enters your mind that it was Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai,
would Rabbi call him just "ben Zakkai"?
phrases.notes: 'רבי' here means רבי יהודה הנשיא, who arranged the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 44.
steps.raayaObject: That בן זכאי is not רבן יוחנן בן זכאי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The plain name used in the משנה, with no title.

steps.title: A ברייתא names רבן יוחנן בן זכאי outright
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says clearly that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי asked about the fig stems. This knocks down the idea of a different בן זכאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: There was an incident, and רבן יוחנן בן זכאי questioned the witnesses about the stems of figs!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 44 with a source that gives the famous sage's full name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא tells the same fig-stem story and names רבן יוחנן בן זכאי himself. So the answer that it was 'some other בן זכאי' cannot stand, and the timing problem comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught? (bringing a source to challenge)

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֶׂה וּבָדַק רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
phrases.english: An incident occurred, and Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai examined the witnesses
about the stems of figs!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: מַעֲשֶׂה וּבָדַק רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 44.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that בן זכאי was a different person.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא names רבן יוחנן בן זכאי himself as the one who asked about the fig stems.

steps.title: He was a student at the time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was then a student sitting before his teacher, and his point made sense to the judges.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he was a student sitting before his teacher. He said something, and his reasoning made sense to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer. The case happened years earlier, when רבן יוחנן בן זכאי was only a student. The sentence continues in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Back then, the סנהדרין was still judging capital cases. So the timing problem goes away. He was not one of the judges, but the judges liked his question and used it. That is why the משנה calls him only 'בן זכאי.'

keyTerms.meaning: A student sitting before his teacher
His reasoning made sense to them

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean he was a judge on the case. He was a student, and the judges adopted his question.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, תַּלְמִיד הַיּוֹשֵׁב לִפְנֵי רַבּוֹ הֲוָה,
phrases.english: Rather, he was a student sitting before his teacher,
and he said something,
and his reasoning made sense to them,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, תַּלְמִיד הַיּוֹשֵׁב לִפְנֵי רַבּוֹ הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 46 and solves the timing problem from steps 41 to 43.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Places the event at an earlier time
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He questioned the witnesses as a leading judge, after the time when capital cases had already stopped.
steps.terutzMaskana: He questioned them as a student, back when the סנהדרין still judged capital cases, and the judges adopted his reasoning.
